claims.quote: You can ask the CMS to set up your child maintenance arrangement online or by phone.
claims.note: Citizens Advice says you can apply to the CMS online, and GOV.UK says the online tool lets you apply.

claims.quote: If you cannot use the ‘Get help arranging child maintenance’ tool, call the Child Maintenance Service .
claims.note: The text says to call the Child Maintenance Service if you cannot use the online tool.

claims.claim: The paying parent's income details are needed.
claims.quote: If you do not have day-to-day care of the child, you’ll also be asked about: your employment details your income and any benefits you get
claims.note: The parent without day-to-day care is asked about their income.

claims.claim: The CMS gets the paying parent's income directly from HMRC.
claims.quote: The Child Maintenance Service will find out the paying parent’s yearly gross income from information supplied by HM Revenue and Customs ( HMRC ).
claims.note: The text says CMS uses HMRC information for the paying parent's income.

claims.claim: You need to give the children's details.
claims.quote: your child’s name and date of birth
claims.note: Citizens Advice lists the child's name and date of birth as information to give the CMS.

claims.claim: You need to give your contact details.
claims.quote: You’ll need to give the CMS detailed information about yourself and your family.
claims.note: The text says you give information about yourself but does not list contact details specifically.
